title: CINM (Cinnamon): A Compilation Infrastructure for Heterogeneous Compute In-Memory and Compute Near-Memory Paradigms
problem: Conventional von-Neumann architectures struggle to meet off-chip memory bandwidth demands for data-intensive applications. Programmability of compute-in-memory and compute-near-memory systems is severely limited by low-level, device-specific programming models.
motivation: Recent CIM and CNM innovations achieve orders-of-magnitude improvements in performance and energy, but require better compiler abstractions to enable practical heterogeneous deployment.
method: CINM builds a compilation system that translates programs into efficient code for compute-in-memory (CIM) and compute-near-memory (CNM) systems—hardware that processes data right where it's stored to avoid bandwidth bottlenecks. It uses hierarchical abstraction layers that work across different CIM and CNM designs, enabling optimizations that either work on any device (device-agnostic) or are customized for specific hardware (device-aware). The system progressively rewrites programs through multiple compilation steps, optimizing at each stage. It was tested on UPMEM (a real CNM system) and memristor-based CIM accelerators.
key_novelty: This is the first compiler using abstraction layers to create optimizations that work across different compute-in-memory and compute-near-memory hardware, rather than requiring hardware-specific optimization for each device.
contributions: End-to-end compilation flow for heterogeneous CIM and CNM paradigms
Hierarchical abstraction framework supporting multiple hardware targets
Progressive lowering pipeline with multi-level optimizations
Practical evaluation on real CNM and CIM hardware with competitive performance

metrics.speedup: comparable to or better than state-of-the-art implementations
metrics.other: orders-of-magnitude improvements in performance and energy consumption
